data.cultural_impact: The name Wardaa holds a significant cultural impact as it signifies perpetual flow and continuous change, a fundamental aspect of life echoing the dynamic nature of Islamic culture and the movements and transformations within it.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Wardaa represents the ongoing river of spiritual growth and nourishment. It is a reminder of the unending journey of the soul towards self-realization and tawheed, as well as an embodiment of Allah's endless mercy and forgiveness. Embracing change and growth in one's spiritual path is emphasized in the Islamic faith, and the name Wardaa reflects this idea of ongoing enlightenment and transformation.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 10, page 562 The name Wardaa carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Wardaa bint Zaid ibn Harithah was the wife of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) for a short period of time. She was a noblewoman of the Khawla bint Hakim tribe and married the Prophet (pbuh) when he was around 53 years old. This marriage was not consummated and was annulled due to Wardaa's illness. She later converted to Christianity and was known as Umm Habibah al-Sawdaa in the Christian community.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd's Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, Volume 3, page 125 The name Wardaa carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Umm Salama bint Abdullah ibn Abu Salama was another woman known as Wardaa. She was an Ansari woman from Banu Harith ibn Ka'b tribe, and she married the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) when she was around 22 years old. This marriage was consummated and produced no offspring. Umm Salama remained with the Prophet (pbuh) until his death.
